answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a scarce token in an on-chain registry, then slash that deposit when a randomly selected audit proves the agent fabricated work or double-claimed a reward. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund each fake identity separately and keep capital immobilized; creating a thousand hollow accounts is no longer free. The token’s violet badge or raven-themed profile adds no protection—the deterrent is the verifiable stake and the risk of losing it.
